text.p: Caterpillar Inc said Tuesday margin as a percent of sales rose to 25 percent in the third quarter from 19 percent a year ago.
The increase was primarily due to higher price realization, stronger volume and the effects of a stronger U.S. dollar, Caterpillar said in a news release.
Continuing improvements in manufacturing efficiencies and essentially flat material costs also helped boost margins, the company said.
An unfavorable product sales mix partially offset the favorable items, the heavy equipment maker said.

Caterpillar also said sales inside the United States were $1.83 billion in the third quarter, up $193 million from a year ago, while sales outside the United States were $2.02 billion, up $88 million from a year ago.
Earlier Tuesday, Caterpillar reported third quarter net income of $310 million, or $1.61 a share, compared with $213 million, or $1.07 a year ago.
The earnings exceeded the First Call mean estimate of $1.34 a share. The range of estimates was $1.10-$1.70, according to First Call.
Higher machine sales in the United States accounted most for a five percent increase in sales voluem in the quarter, Caterpillar said.

Prices improved pirmarily due to price increases taken in the past year, the absence of certain European currency hedges that were in place a year ago and a favorable change in geographic sales mix, the company said.

Selling, general and administrative expenses rose to $423 million from $352 a year ago, due to higher incentive pay expense, inflation and increased spending to support expanded operations, Caterpillar said. The 1995 figure included a favorable adjustment to insurance reserves.
U.S. dealer machine sales to end-users declined due to a reduced share of industry sales, Caterpillar said.
Deliveries to U.S. dealer rental fleets declined from a year ago, as rental inventories remained above year-ago levels, the company said.

Dealer machine sales in Europe were lower due to declines in Germany and France, where the contruction sector remains weak, the company said. Sales in China, Japan, Australia and Latin America were up, while sales in Canada were unchanged and sales fell in the Commonwealth of Independent States.
Caterpillar shares rose 1-1/4 to 75-3/8 Tuesday morning.
